members.name: institutional_flow_momentum_v1
members.thesis: Large individual bar volume spikes (>5x SMA(volume,20)) that move price by >0.2% in one direction likely represent institutional block execution or large algo orders. These create temporary momentum because: (1) the large order itself moves the price, (2) other algos detect the large print and follo
members.exit_stop: 0.2% from entry OR price crosses back to the open of the spike bar (impact fully reversed)
filters: no specific filter — institutional flows occur regardless of VIX
vol_spike > 5x is the core filter (very strict)
VWAP direction should confirm the spike direction
weaknesses: Not all volume spikes are institutional — could be ETF rebalancing, bulk deal, or single large retail order
The 5x volume threshold is very strict, reducing trade frequency to 1-2 per day across the universe
Entry is 2 bars after the spike — by then, initial price impact may have already decayed, entering after the best move
members.prior_art: Institutional flow detection: Kyle (1985) informed trading model. Volume spike analysis: Karpoff (1987) 'Relation Between Price Changes and Trading Volume'. Momentum ignition: Brogaard et al. (2014) '

members.name: trade_size_clustering_v1
members.thesis: Institutional orders in Indian equities are often split into round-lot sizes (multiples of 100 or 500 shares) via TWAP/VWAP algorithms. When we detect clusters of trades at consistent round-lot sizes within a rolling window, it signals institutional accumulation or distribution. The inefficiency per
filters: no filter (institutional flow persists across volatility regimes)
skip first 5 min and last 10 min of session
align with NIFTY 50 intraday trend (above/below index VWAP)
weaknesses: Tick-level trade data in India is expensive and not available via standard Zerodha API. NSE TBT data feed required, adding infrastructure cost.
Institutional algos are increasingly randomizing trade sizes to avoid detection, directly degrading the round_lot_ratio signal quality.
False positives from retail traders who also trade round lots (especially in lower-priced stocks where 100 shares is a small notional).
members.prior_art: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity' (VPIN). Hasbrouck (2007) 'Empirical Market Microstructure' covers trade classification. Kyle (1985) 'Continuous Auctions and Inside
